content: Search the JI repository read-only for any existing production mechanism to register/load custom tools or extensions into JiCli/HostComposition/standalone (ServiceLoader, plugin modules, extension manifests, built-in test profile), and any performance test architecture that launches the standalone distribution while injecting a faux provider. Also inspect ToolBatchScheduler ordering semantics to determine whether 16 simultaneous effects can be achieved using existing built-in read/write/edit/shell tools across two Sessions. Return concise findings with exact file:line anchors and best minimal approach. Do not modify files. Search breadth: very thorough.
title: Agent prompt

content:
## Findings

### 1. No production custom-tool/plugin loader exists for CLI/standalone

The only implemented `ServiceLoader` seam selects the internal Agent runtime implementation:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\AgentRuntimeBuilder.java:63-77` builds `RuntimeConfiguration`, then loads the first `AgentRuntimeFactory`.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\AgentRuntimeBuilder.java:80-83` describes that SPI as an internal implementation seam.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\resources\META-INF\services\io.github.diodeme.ji.agent.AgentRuntimeBuilder$AgentRuntimeFactory:1` registers only `CoreAgentRuntimeFactory`.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\CoreAgentRuntimeFactory.java:7-11` simply constructs Core.

It is not a provider/tool/plugin discovery mechanism. There is:

- no implemented `ToolProvider` type,
- no production extension-directory scanner,
- no plugin/extension manifest,
- no JPMS `module-info.java`,
- no standalone `ClassLoader`/`URLClassLoader` extension path,
- no implemented `JI_TEST_PROFILE` switch. `JI_TEST_PROFILE` appears only as documentation at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\docs\java-rewrite\09-development-environment.md:130-139`.

The design document proposes a `ToolProvider` and approved-JAR loading, but this remains aspirational:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\docs\java-rewrite\03-java-modules-and-extension-spi.md:143-160`
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\docs\java-rewrite\03-java-modules-and-extension-spi.md:172-182`

Spring also exposes no injection route: it calls the ordinary environment-only `LocalHostApplication.open` at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-spring-boot-starter\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\spring\JiHostAutoConfiguration.java:19-23`, while its public surface is intentionally restricted at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-spring-boot-starter\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\spring\JiHost.java:5-11`.

### 2. Injection exists, but only through package-private test/composition seams

The composition supports injected providers and additional tools internally:

- Default plus additional tool registration:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\HostComposition.java:110-120`
- `additionalTools` in package-private `HostComposition.Options`:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\HostComposition.java:381-402`
- Provider/tool-aware composition overload:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\JiCli.java:148-155`
- Injected provider replaces built-in provider construction:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\JiCli.java:212-223`
- Package-private Host overload accepting provider and tools:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\LocalHostApplication.java:37-52`

The only public production Host opening method accepts environment alone:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\LocalHostApplication.java:32-35`

The standalone entry point consequently has no injection route:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-standalone\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\standalone\JiStandalone.java:15-37`, especially the environment-only call at line 30.

The embedded API does publicly support explicit custom tools through `AgentRuntimeBuilder.tool`:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\AgentRuntimeBuilder.java:48-61`

That helps embedded consumers, not `JiCli` or the standalone launcher.

### 3. Current performance gate does not launch the standalone distribution

The Stage 6 test harness deliberately bridges into the package-private seam by declaring itself in the CLI package:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\Stage6HostHarness.java:1`
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\Stage6HostHarness.java:21-24`

`Stage6Performance` then starts that Host in-process with a `ScriptedModelProvider` and eight custom blocking tools:

- In-process setup and assertion of 16 entered effects:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\stage6\Stage6Performance.java:47-65`
- Two scripted turns, each emitting eight tool calls:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\stage6\Stage6Performance.java:124-141`
- Eight non-sequential, always-allowed latch-blocking tools:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\stage6\Stage6Performance.java:150-161`
- Two Sessions are activated through two HCP clients:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\test-support\ji-stage6-testkit\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\stage6\Stage6Performance.java:163-166`

The release script builds a standalone archive, but runs a separate testkit distribution:

- Standalone archive build:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage6-ubuntu-release.ps1:83-105`
- Testkit distribution is separately archived:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage6-ubuntu-release.ps1:41-43`
- Performance container executes `Stage6Testkit`, not `ji-host` or `JiStandalone`:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\run-stage6-ubuntu-release.ps1:161-167`

Likewise, the Stage 4 standalone gate only builds/unpacks and inspects the launcher/runtime; it never starts the Host:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\scripts\verify-stage4-standalone.ps1:13-27`

Thus there is currently no architecture that launches the produced standalone distribution while injecting an in-process faux provider.

### 4. ToolBatchScheduler ordering and concurrency

Semantics are explicit:

- Default limits are 8 active effects per Session, 32 per Host, queue 1,024:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchScheduler.java:25-29`
- Every request completes preflight in input order before any effect is scheduled:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchScheduler.java:69-82`
- If any item evaluates as sequential, the entire batch is chained serially; otherwise all effects are submitted:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchScheduler.java:126-141`
- Admission scans in queue order but skips a session at its limit, allowing later eligible Sessions through; it is therefore work-conserving rather than strict global FIFO:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchScheduler.java:165-181`
- Results retain request order even though non-sequential effects may finish in any order:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchScheduler.java:140-142`
- The scheduler is shared by every Session in one runtime:  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\CoreAgentRuntime.java:26-48`

Tests directly verify ordered preflight, whole-batch serialization, and per-Session/Host admission:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\test\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchSchedulerTest.java:36-70`
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\test\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\ToolBatchSchedulerTest.java:74-115`

One active run is allowed per Session, but different Sessions run concurrently:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-agent-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\agent\core\CoreAgentSession.java:64-95`

### 5. Can built-ins produce 16 simultaneous effects across two Sessions?

**Theoretically yes with read-only batches; deterministically no with the current built-ins.**

Built-in definitions are:

- `read`: `sequential=false`
- `write`, `edit`, `shell`: `sequential=true`

Anchors:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\WorkspaceTools.java:18-42`
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\WorkspaceTools.java:45-82`

The CLI policy independently enforces the same rule: only `read` is non-sequential:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\JiCli.java:249-258`

Consequences:

- Two Sessions, each receiving one model turn containing eight `read` calls, can occupy 8 + 8 = 16 scheduler slots.
- Any batch containing `write`, `edit`, or `shell` becomes wholly serial. Across two Sessions that means at most two such effects are executing simultaneously, one per Session.
- A blocking `shell` command cannot create eight resident effects per Session because its whole batch is serialized.
- Built-in reads have no controllable latch. They perform ordinary synchronous file reads at  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\LocalWorkspaceProvider.java:96-117`.  
  Eight reads may overlap briefly, but cannot reliably remain resident long enough for an authoritative “16 simultaneous effects” assertion.
- Built-ins use `ASK`; preflight resolves requests serially before effects start, so a test must approve each read permission before the batch is released to execution. Custom Stage 6 tools avoid this with `alwaysAllow()`.

Also, the current Stage 6 test proves that 16 effects are resident, but it does not prove a Host maximum of 16: production still uses the scheduler’s default Host limit of 32.

## Best minimal approach

1. **Do not repurpose the internal `AgentRuntimeFactory` ServiceLoader seam.** Selection is `findFirst()`, and it is explicitly intended only to keep Core implementation types out of the public builder.
2. **For the smallest reliable performance correction, unpack the standalone distribution and launch a small Stage 6 child bootstrap using its bundled Java and exact `lib/*`.** Put that bootstrap in `io.github.diodeme.ji.cli` so it can reuse the existing package-private `LocalHostApplication.open(environment, provider, ports, tools)` seam. Move the current scripted provider and eight latch-blocking tools into that child; let the controller drive the two HCP Sessions and collect OS/container metrics.
3. This exercises the packaged runtime, production jars, Host composition, transports, persistence, and scheduler without inventing a fake production plugin system. It does not literally enter through `JiStandalone.main`; if that exact entry point is mandatory, a new intentional injection contract is required.
4. An external OpenAI-compatible faux HTTP server can make the unmodified `JiStandalone` exercise its real provider adapter, but it does not solve deterministic blocking-tool injection.
5. Using eight built-in reads per Session is acceptable only for a lightweight concurrency smoke. It is not a robust replacement for the current latch-based 16-resident-effect gate.

### 5. Can built-ins produce 16 simultaneous effects across two Sessions?

**Theoretically yes with read-only batches; deterministically no with the current built-ins.**

Built-in definitions are:

- `read`: `sequential=false`
- `write`, `edit`, `shell`: `sequential=true`

Anchors:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\WorkspaceTools.java:18-42`
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\WorkspaceTools.java:45-82`

The CLI policy independently enforces the same rule: only `read` is non-sequential:

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\products\ji-cli\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\cli\JiCli.java:249-258`

Consequences:

- Two Sessions, each receiving one model turn containing eight `read` calls, can occupy 8 + 8 = 16 scheduler slots.
- Any batch containing `write`, `edit`, or `shell` becomes wholly serial. Across two Sessions that means at most two such effects are executing simultaneously, one per Session.
- A blocking `shell` command cannot create eight resident effects per Session because its whole batch is serialized.
- Built-in reads have no controllable latch. They perform ordinary synchronous file reads at  
  `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-workspace-local\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\workspace\local\LocalWorkspaceProvider.java:96-117`.  
  Eight reads may overlap briefly, but cannot reliably remain resident long enough for an authoritative “16 simultaneous effects” assertion.
- Built-ins use `ASK`; preflight resolves requests serially before effects start, so a test must approve each read permission before the batch is released to execution. Custom Stage 6 tools avoid this with `alwaysAllow()`.

Also, the current Stage 6 test proves that 16 effects are resident, but it does not prove a Host maximum of 16: production still uses the scheduler’s default Host limit of 32.

## Best minimal approach

1. **Do not repurpose the internal `AgentRuntimeFactory` ServiceLoader seam.** Selection is `findFirst()`, and it is explicitly intended only to keep Core implementation types out of the public builder.
2. **For the smallest reliable performance correction, unpack the standalone distribution and launch a small Stage 6 child bootstrap using its bundled Java and exact `lib/*`.** Put that bootstrap in `io.github.diodeme.ji.cli` so it can reuse the existing package-private `LocalHostApplication.open(environment, provider, ports, tools)` seam. Move the current scripted provider and eight latch-blocking tools into that child; let the controller drive the two HCP Sessions and collect OS/container metrics.
3. This exercises the packaged runtime, production jars, Host composition, transports, persistence, and scheduler without inventing a fake production plugin system. It does not literally enter through `JiStandalone.main`; if that exact entry point is mandatory, a new intentional injection contract is required.
4. An external OpenAI-compatible faux HTTP server can make the unmodified `JiStandalone` exercise its real provider adapter, but it does not solve deterministic blocking-tool injection.
5. Using eight built-in reads per Session is acceptable only for a lightweight concurrency smoke. It is not a robust replacement for the current latch-based 16-resident-effect gate.
